timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hi, this is State Representative Tim O'Brien and I'm the Democratic nominee for mayor.
I'm running for mayor of New Britain because I want the people of our community to believe
in a brighter future. There is so much that is possible, whether it is creating good-paying
jobs for our city's future. Proving our tax base so that we can make sure that we're
taking the burden off of homeowners when it comes to property taxes, making sure that
we are investing in our education system so that our kids will have a brighter future
and our city will have a brighter future too, and improving neighborhood quality of life
so that every neighborhood on our city is a quality place to live in. There's so much
that is possible and it's not hard, but it is hard work. There are solid policies we
can institute to achieve all of these different things and I know this and that's why I'm
running for mayor. Let's talk about jobs. When it comes to job creation, there should
be an action plan that we as a community are a part of building. All of the places that
are available for development in our city should have a plan for what kind of business
we want to set up there and we should have a plan for how we're going to achieve each
and every one of those plans of development. One of the most important things we need to
do is to help people who live in our community to start their own new businesses. We should
encourage local spending so that we are creating jobs with the dollars that we spend in taxpayer
dollars and help people to spend locally as well so that together we can be building jobs
for our city's future. That kind of strong action plan, not just waiting for good things
to come our way, the way city hall has been doing, but making sure that it happens. So that's
what we need to do to build up business and create jobs. That grows the grand list so
we can reduce the burden on homeowners when it comes to property taxes. But there's
something else we need to do to reduce the burden on homeowners when it comes to property
taxes and that shifting the burden back on to blended building owners. And so what they
effectively are doing, when you as a responsible homeowner are taking care of your property,
when revaluation time comes for property taxes, your house is valued as a well-maintained
house and their building is maintained as an irresponsibly run falling apart building.
So they give themselves a tax break. It's wrong. That's why as a state legislator I approve
legislation to allow the city to apply something called an anti-blight assessment to shift
the burden off of homeowners and people who live in our community and the businesses that
are doing the right thing in our community and back on to those irresponsible property
owners. Everybody in our city regardless of their lot in life, whether you are, whether
you are very wealthy, middle class or are very humble means, you should all have the right
to live in a decent and quality neighborhood. There should be no lines that are drawn when
it comes to quality of life and we should make sure that everybody has a good quality of
life and a decent neighborhood to live in, to raise their children and to grow old.
Now when it comes to education, this should be one of the highest priorities in our city.
It's so important for our city's future not just to improve the quality of education
because it's the right thing to do for our city's kids but because it's the right thing
to do for our city's future. There are too many people who pick up states, move out of
our city because they don't want to send their kids to our city schools. Other people
who might consider settling in our city choose not to because they don't want to send their
kids to our city's schools. Now there are a lot of good-hearted people who do a good job
for our city's kids. They work their hard out to provide a good quality education but
the truth is that the quality of the education needs to be a higher priority in our city
halls budget. It ultimately hurts our economy. It hurts the tax base because property values
for homeowners go down when people choose not to live in our city because of the quality
of our schools and it hurts our city's future in so many different intangible ways. We
have to do the right thing in investing in our education. Now we need to move away from
pointing fingers when it comes to education of saying this person or that person is responsible
for that education and talk about how we're going to work together as a community. So there's
so much that it's possible for our city's future. I want the people of our city to believe
that we can have a brighter future for our community and to believe that there are good
strong policies that we can bring in our city hall to be able to make that happen. As
your mayor I'm going to be working with you. This is not going to be a city hall that's
going to be all about one person. It's going to be about you. As a together as a community
we can achieve so much for our community's future. I'm so proud to be the Democratic nominee
for mayor and I'm going to be very proud to be working with you as your mayor. Thank you
so much. I'm Tim O'Brien and I approve this message because I believe in New Britain's
future.
